chapter_answers.q3_what_adjudication_adds: ORDERING + PROBES + FAILURE MODES THAT NO LANE CAN SEE FROM INSIDE ITS ASK. The 09-29 glm-5.3-prime judgment (watch/inbox/HERMES_PRIME_JUDGMENT_20260929.md, 304 prompt / 6,277 completion tokens, $0.0560888 banked) took raw findings and returned a strict sequence under an exposure clock: rotate the key before snapshotting or the backup exports the leak; probe per move (old key must 401, restore-test the pack, first mapped find must move an eval); named failure modes (backup-as-decoration, knowledge theater, cadence nobody reads). Each of those is a cross-lane property: no single lane ranks exposures or sees the sequencing hazard. This run's own hermes-judgment lane was in flight (dispatch_prime pending) at read time; the precedent is the byte evidence.
chapter_answers.q4_standing_wave_verdict: YES, A WEEKLY SLOT, BUT AS A DEPTH INSTRUMENT NOT A VOLUME RITUAL. The loop demonstrably compounds where it converts (audits to gates to law; corpus fold to steal vocabulary; register to same-night fills) and demonstrably circles where it only produces (laws-to-ribs frozen at 2, D falling while receipts grow, salon-mine synthesis stalled). A weekly slot that reruns tools/ouroboros.py and diffs volume only would ratify the circle. The slot earns its place iff it diffs depth (D, the three thin_edges lines, receipts absorbed that week) and spends its one-sitting on the thinnest edge, starting with rib-minting from absorbed receipts and closing salon-mine's m20.
